KEY MESSAGE 1...
Upper level troughing continues across much of the eastern CONUS and 
north into Eastern Canada and will slowly deepen off to the east 
throughout the weekend. Meanwhile, shortwave features are expected 
to move north to south along the western periphery of the trough 
bringing reinforcing upper level support and colder air into the 
region. 850mb and 500mb temperatures have bottomed out at around -6C 
and -25 to -30C, respectively, this morning and will be steady 
through the overnight before gradually warming throughout the day 
Saturday. 

Currently, flow is out of the north across the region allowing for a 
lake effect band to set up from Erie Co, OH south trough Knox Co. 
Generally, this band has been primarily rain with some rain/snow 
showers mixed in. Given the flow, this band has been able to tap 
into the moisture from Lake Huron, and to a lesser extent, Lake St. 
Clair. Flow will begin to shift to be out of the north to northwest 
this evening into Saturday and as a result, the band will shift to 
the east towards the Cleveland metro area. There will be a 
reinforcing vort max moving south as the flow does shift that will 
help in giving the band more strength. Temperatures will also drop 
to the coldest expected this weekend with lows in the upper 20s to 
low 30s and the lake shore staying in the mid to upper 30s. With the 
areas near the shore being warmer, and any precipitation that falls 
is expected to stay as rain through the overnight hours. Further 
south away from the lake shore where the temperatures are colder and 
the elevation rises, rain will transition over to a rain/snow mix 
overnight. There will be periods of only snow, but expect it to be 
mainly a mix. Light accumulations are possible as well, though with 
the ground being fairly warm, it will limit the overall totals.
There may be some areas across Northeastern Ohio and 
Northwestern Pennsylvania that could see around an inch or two 
of accumulation by tomorrow morning but expect those 
occurrences to be isolated. 

Throughout the day Saturday, flow will continue to shift to be more 
northwesterly and veer to be more west of north further up in the 
column. This will create a more multi-banded set up impacting 
Northeastern Ohio and Northwestern Pennsylvania throughout the day. 
There will still be some support from the Lake Huron connection but 
drier, low-level air will start to push in from the west as the
trough begins to push east and the ridge builds in from the 
west. Temperatures will rise into the mid 40s tomorrow as well, 
so expect precipitation to fall mainly as rain after the morning
hours. A final, vort max will move south through the region 
late Saturday night into Sunday morning that will reinvigorate 
the lake effect band with additional moisture through Sunday 
morning. With temperatures warming, and staying above freezing 
for much of the region, expecting this precipitation to stay as 
rain overnight. There will be some exceptions as the higher 
elevations of Northwest Pennsylvania could see some rain/snow 
mix, but with little to no accumulation. 

Lingering lake effect rain showers are possible across Northeastern 
Ohio and Northwestern Pennsylvania throughout Sunday and into early 
Monday morning as there will be some low level moisture across that 
area. Elsewhere, should begin to see the lake effect cloud cover 
begin to dissipate Sunday night through Monday as the 925mb and
850mb ridges build east across the region. Dry weather is 
expected across the region after Monday morning with high 
pressure building in.

KEY MESSAGE 2... 
The upper level trough will exit to the east Sunday night into 
Monday as an upper level ridge builds in across the Northern Great 
Plains into the Great Lakes regions. This will build eastward 
through the early part of next week as a more amplified ridge 
builds across the Rockies and progresses eastward. All that 
being said, surface high pressure will build in from the 
northwest into the Ohio Valley Monday through the middle of the
week with dry, quiet weather expected. Temperatures will start 
off chilly to begin the week with high in the upper 40s to low 
50s and progressively warm as the high builds east and the 
region moves into southwesterly flow. By Thursday, highs will be
more seasonable, if not a few degrees warmer, in the upper 50s 
to low 60s. Overnight lows will follow a similar pattern,
starting off in the mid to upper 20s and warm into the 30s by 
mid week.
